requirement:
Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
rationale:
structural: The text has one structural obligation: the definition input form is a stored data shape. The clause is "a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`". An implementation that stored extra fields, such as a line number, or omitted `text` would violate it. The roots cover that shape in three places.

- `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[to_input]` produces `{definition, text}` for the `Definition` variant.
- `src/evidence_format.rs#fn[check_shape]` requires `object.len() == 2` with `definition` as a string and `text` as a string array for `Definition` inputs.
- `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_input]` calls `check_keys` with exactly `["definition", "text"]` when the input has a `definition` key.

The remaining clauses specify observable behavior only, so they create no structural obligation:

- `text` holds the complete raw declaration as source lines.
- Validation rejects missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifies the definition, and shows a diff.
- Moving an unchanged definition does not invalidate its snapshot.
- Displays show the name, current location, and recorded text.

Any implementation that produces these results meets them. `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[resolve]` is where the raw-line text and the missing-definition error are produced. The text names no particular library, algorithm, or interface for these clauses.

The `InputSelector::Definition` variant is reached from the marked roots, so it needs no separate marker. I found no structural obligation without implementation evidence.

behavioral: Obligations and the tests that cover them:

- **Exact form (`definition` and `text` only).** `tests/definitions.rs#fn[definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked]` adds an `unexpected` field to a definition input and asserts an "unexpected field" error.
- **`text` is required.** `tests/definitions.rs#fn[changed_definition_snapshots_show_a_compact_diff_and_text_is_required]` removes `text`, sets it to `[]` and sets it to a string. It asserts that each case is rejected with an error on the record that mentions `text`.
- **Complete raw fenced declaration.** The `declaration` helper records the whole block, from the `:::{definition}` line through the closing `:::`, including the phrase option and body. The tests pass validation with those snapshots. They also reject changes to the phrase option (`glossary.b`) and to the body (`glossary.a`).
- **`definition` identifies one named definition; missing definitions are rejected.** Four tests show this:
  - `definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked` deletes `md/glossary.md` and asserts "no matching named definition" for `glossary.a`.
  - `changed_definition_snapshots_show_a_compact_diff_and_text_is_required` uses a requirement name and an example name as definition inputs. It asserts the same error for each.
  - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configuration_and_dependency_failures_do_not_stop_later_checks]` uses `rules.gone`, which does not exist, and asserts the error.
  - `cyclic_dependencies_are_required_once_and_changes_require_review` checks missing and duplicate inputs.
- **Changed snapshot text is rejected, names the definition and shows a compact diff.** `changed_definition_snapshots_show_a_compact_diff_and_text_is_required` asserts that the error names `glossary.a`. It also asserts that the diff lines after the first are exactly a removal of the old body line and an addition of the new one. `cyclic_dependencies_are_required_once_and_changes_require_review` checks three further edits and asserts that the error names the right definition each time.
- **Moving an unchanged definition does not invalidate the snapshot.** `cyclic_dependencies_are_required_once_and_changes_require_review` prepends blank lines to `glossary.md`, which shifts both definitions. It asserts that validation still has no errors.
- **Evidence displays show name, current source location and recorded text.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group]` asserts that the detail page shows the definition name, then its file and inclusive range, then the recorded text block, in that order.

I found no obligation without a test.
